'''William Parry Murphy Jr.''' (November 11, 1923 – November 30, 2023) was an American physician and inventor of medical devices including collaborating on a flexible sealed blood bag used for [[blood transfusion]]s. He was the son of the American physician [[William Parry Murphy]] who shared the [[Nobel Prize in Physiology]] for Medicine in 1934,<ref>{{cite web|title=Biography|url=https://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/medicine/laureates/1934/murphy-bio.html|work=nobelprize.org|accessdate=December 30, 2010}}</ref> and Harriett Adams, the first licensed female dentist in Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lemelson-MIT|url=http://web.mit.edu/invent/n-pressreleases/n-press-03LAABG.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20031011233011/http://web.mit.edu/invent/n-pressreleases/n-press-03LAABG.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 11, 2003|accessdate=November 7, 2013}}</ref>

==Background==
William Parry Murphy Jr. was born in Boston on November 11, 1923, the son of hematologist [[William Parry Murphy]] and Harriet (née Adams) Murphy, the first woman to become a licensed dentist in Massachusetts.<ref name = McFadden>{{cite news|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2023/12/05/science/william-p-murphy-jr-dead.html|title = William P. Murphy Jr., an Inventor of the Modern Blood Bag, Dies at 100|last = McFadden|first = Robert D.|authorlink = Robert D. McFadden|date = December 5, 2023|accessdate = December 5, 2023|newspaper = [[The New York Times]]|url-access = limited}}</ref> Murphy grew up in [[Brookline, Massachusetts]].<ref name = McFadden/> He graduated from [[Harvard University]] in 1946 with a major in pre-medicine and a minor in architecture. He received his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] in 1947 from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]] and also studied physiologic instrumentation at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1947 to 1948.<ref name = McFadden/>

===Personal life===
Murphy married Barbara Eastham in 1943; they had three daughters and divorced in the early 1970s.<ref name = McFadden/> In 1973, he married Beverly Patterson.<ref name = McFadden/>

Murphy turned 100 on November 11, 2023, and died 19 days later, on November 30, at his home in [[Coral Gables, Florida]].<ref name = McFadden/>

==Career==
Murphy was the chairman of the board of directors at U.S. Stem Cell, formerly Bioheart. He retired in 2022.<ref name="McFadden" />

===U.S. Patents===

Murphy holds 17 U.S. patents issued between 1952 and 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://patft.uspto.gov/netahtml/PTO/srchnum.htm |title=US Patent and TradeMark Office Patent Search |access-date=July 12, 2013 |archive-date=April 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190428053810/http://patft.uspto.gov/netahtml/PTO/srchnum.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Publications==
He co-authored nearly 30 medical publications and helped to establish several professional organizations such as [[For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology|FIRST]] (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology), a non-profit group dedicated to inspiring young people's interest in science, technology and engineering, founded by his friend [[Dean Kamen]].
